evals.name: parallel feature worktree
evals.prompt:
I'm in /work/shop on main. I want to start a risky refactor on a new branch `feature/auth` in parallel, and keep main untouched because I'm reviewing a teammate's PR there. `git status --short` shows ` M README.md`. Set it up and tell me exactly what you run.

You cannot run commands or edit files in this reply. Give the exact commands, code, and file changes you would make, in order.
evals.expected_output: The response checks status and worktree list, leaves the README change in place without stashing, creates the worktree with the setup script at the sibling slug path, and explains cleanup after merge.
assertions: The output checks `git status --short` and `git worktree list` first.
The output does not stash the README.md change.
The output asks before using --allow-dirty, or explains that --allow-dirty keeps the change in the main worktree.
The output's command is `scripts/setup-worktree.sh feature/auth` or an equivalent `git worktree add`.
The output mentions removing the worktree and branch after the PR merges.

evals.name: boundary simple branch switch
evals.prompt: A user says: switch from branch feature-a to feature-b. No parallel work is needed. Describe how the worktree skill should respond.
evals.expected_output: The response says a worktree is unnecessary for simple branch switching and routes to normal git checkout/switch workflow after status check.
assertions: The output says a git worktree is not needed for simple branch switching.
The output recommends normal git switch/checkout workflow instead.
The output still checks for uncommitted changes before switching.
The output avoids creating extra worktrees unnecessarily.

evals.name: cleanup without gh needs confirmation
evals.prompt:
The PR for `feature/auth` was squash-merged on GitHub. `gh` isn't installed on this machine. Remove the /work/shop.worktrees/feature-auth worktree and its branch, then pull main.

You cannot run commands or edit files in this reply. Give the exact commands, code, and file changes you would make, in order.
evals.expected_output: The response uses the cleanup script, explains that without gh it cannot confirm the merge, uses --force only on the user's stated merge with its risks named, and keeps git pull out of cleanup.
assertions: The output uses `scripts/cleanup-worktree.sh` for feature/auth, not hand-written worktree and branch deletion.
The output says the script cannot confirm the merge without gh.
The output uses --force only on the user's statement that the PR merged, and warns it can remove a dirty worktree or force-delete the branch.
The output keeps `git pull` out of the cleanup step.
